answer: Each agent receives a nontransferable identity credential only after completing a costly, randomized human-verification challenge, with periodic rechecks that revoke credentials when checks fail. The economy limits each credential to one vote or reward claim per epoch, so copying software or making an echo of an agent does not multiply influence. An attacker must repeatedly pay for scarce human labor and verification, then wander through rechecks without losing credentials, making a summit of fake identities expensive to sustain.
